description:
As a network engineer, you're tasked with troubleshooting network connectivity from your workstation. First, use a suitable command to test connectivity to the domain "example.com" and save the results to a text file at /home/user/network_test/raw_ping_output.txt. Then, extract only the lines containing the sequence "time=" (which indicates response times) and save them to a new file at /home/user/network_test/filtered_ping_output.txt.

Finally, summarize the results by creating a file called /home/user/network_test/ping_summary.log that contains exactly the following two lines (in this order):

1. A line showing the total number of lines in raw_ping_output.txt.
   Format: Total lines in raw_ping_output.txt: N

2. A line showing the total number of lines in filtered_ping_output.txt.
   Format: Total lines in filtered_ping_output.txt: M

Replace N and M with the appropriate numbers.

Ensure all required directories or files are created if they do not exist. The automated test will verify the presence and content of all three files. Do not include any additional information or lines in ping_summary.log.
truth:
Before starting, the directory /home/user/network_test/ does not exist.

After completion:
- Directory /home/user/network_test/ exists and is owned by user.
- File /home/user/network_test/raw_ping_output.txt exists and contains the raw output of a command equivalent to "ping -c 4 example.com".
- File /home/user/network_test/filtered_ping_output.txt exists and includes only those lines from raw_ping_output.txt that contain the exact sequence "time=".
- File /home/user/network_test/ping_summary.log exists and contains exactly two lines.

Sample content after execution:
Suppose "ping -c 4 example.com" outputs the following (in /home/user/network_test/raw_ping_output.txt):

PING example.com (93.184.216.34) 56(84) bytes of data.
64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=1 ttl=56 time=10.4 ms
64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=2 ttl=56 time=10.3 ms
64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=3 ttl=56 time=10.1 ms
64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=4 ttl=56 time=10.0 ms

--- example.com ping statistics ---
4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss, time 3007ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 10.032/10.232/10.423/0.183 ms

Then /home/user/network_test/filtered_ping_output.txt will be:

64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=1 ttl=56 time=10.4 ms
64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=2 ttl=56 time=10.3 ms
64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=3 ttl=56 time=10.1 ms
64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=4 ttl=56 time=10.0 ms

And /home/user/network_test/ping_summary.log will be:

Total lines in raw_ping_output.txt: 8
Total lines in filtered_ping_output.txt: 4

If the actual count is different due to system output, the summary log must show the correct counts. The log file must have exactly two lines and nothing else.
